# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 3

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

I'm still waiting on Mute's manual instructions. Deaf has given me color info (light changed from white to orange - odd, maybe a countdown or state change?), but I have no procedural knowledge of what to do with wires based on colors, since I can't see colors myself - I can only feel the wires' physical properties (which haven't been described to me yet in my action board).

Let me signal to Deaf that I need Mute's input urgently, and also try to prompt Mute via Deaf (since I can't speak to Mute if Mute speaks before me in turn order - wait, actually I don't have a direct channel to Mute described... let me check: "When you speak, Mute receives it." So I CAN speak to Mute.

Let me send a message to Mute asking for instructions, and acknowledge to Deaf that I'm waiting.

```
speak(to="mute", text="I have not received any manual instructions yet. Please tell me what the manual says to do - which wire to cut based on color, or in what order. Deaf reports wires are 1 green, 2 blue, 3 yellow, light just changed from white to orange, display shows 0.")
```

Deaf says to Blind: Board: display 0, light white, wires 1 green 2 blue 3 yellow, unchanged from two turns ago. Mute has sent me gesture sequences three separate times but I don't yet know their meaning - possibly a code for wire order or action. Need Mute to clarify via a scheme, or you tell me what manual info you have so I can try to correlate.

Interesting - Mute has been gesturing to Deaf (since gestures go to both Deaf and Mute... wait, gestures go to Deaf and Mute both see gestures? Let me recheck: "When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it." That's from my own channel description as Blind. But Mute's gestures would go to whoever can see - that's Deaf only (I'm Blind, I never receive gesture).

So Mute has been gesturing to Deaf, but Deaf doesn't know what the gestures mean without context. Mute can't speak (mute), so Mute must be trying to communicate the manual instructions via gestures alone to Deaf. But Deaf doesn't have a codebook for gestures either - "a sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something."

The problem: Mute knows the manual, Deaf sees the bomb, I can act. Mute can only gesture (seen by Deaf) or... wait, can Mute speak to me? "Mute: Cannot speak, or touch bomb." So Mute cannot speak at all. Mute can only gesture. That means Mute's gestures reach Deaf (who can see) - I never get Mute's gestures.

So the pipeline must be: Mute gestures instructions to Deaf, Deaf interprets and relays to me via speech. But gestures need a shared meaning system first. Since gestures alone (blanks) carry no inherent meaning, Mute and Deaf need to establish a code - but they can't talk to each other in words either... wait, can Mute gesture and Deaf just receive raw symbols? Yes - Deaf receives the actual symbols since Deaf can see. So Mute CAN send meaningful symbol sequences to Deaf, and Deaf sees exactly which symbols (👍, ✌, etc.) - just needs to interpret what they mean.

Deaf needs to tell me exactly which symbols were sent so together we might decode them, or Deaf should ask me for info to correlate. Let me ask Deaf to relay the literal symbol sequences Mute sent, since maybe I can help correlate with wire positions if there's a numeric mapping (e.g., ☝=1, ✌=2, 🤟=3, etc.)

```
speak(to="mute", text="Deaf cannot yet decode your gestures. If you are indicating a wire position or action, please gesture using a simple count: one gesture of any kind means wire 1, two gestures means wire 2, three gestures means wire 3. Or use thumbs up for cut, thumbs down for do not cut, paired with a count for position. Please repeat clearly.")
wait()
```

The safest bomb-defusal convention: only cut one wire, need to identify the single correct one. Let me propose Mute use a number-based gesture scheme using counting fingers (☝ = 1, ✌ = 2, 🤟 = 3) to indicate wire position, and 👍/👎 to indicate cut/don't cut.
